name: DFW 1980 to 2000 single-story on slab
description: Single-story slab house built 1980 to 2000, before the first Texas energy code: R-19 attic, R-11 walls, double-pane clear aluminum windows, attic ducts. Every value is an estimate to seed the questionnaire; inspect and override.

era.code_basis: No statewide energy code in Texas before September 2001 (SECO); builder practice only.

sources.citation: RhoeFlow DFW era template research (claude/01-plan/dfw-era-template-research.md), section Era by era: 1980 to 2000. Every value, its range, evidence type and confidence.
Texas SECO, single-family energy code history: no statewide code before September 2001; 2000 IECC 2001-2011; 2009 IRC from 2012; 2015 IRC from September 2016
Huang, Hanford and Yang, LBNL-44636 (1999): West South Central prototype houses, pre-1950 no insulation, 1950-79 R-7 ceiling and uninsulated walls, 1980s R-27 roof and R-11 walls

Chan, Joh and Sherman, Analysis of air leakage measurements of US houses (LBNL, Energy and Buildings 2013): leakage by year built (pre-1960 2.2x post-2000, 1960s 1.9x, 1970s 1.8x, 1980s 1.5x, 1990s 1.15x), vented crawlspace about 24% above slab; NL 0.55 is about 10 ACH50
NREL ResStock housing characteristics (develop branch): Texas and climate zone 3A insulation, window, foundation and infiltration distributions by vintage; duct leakage and insulation are assumptions

IECC 2015 Tables R303.1.3(1) and R303.1.3(3), default U-factor and SHGC for unlabeled windows: metal single 1.20, metal double 0.80, nonmetal single 0.95; SHGC single clear 0.8, double clear 0.7 (Seattle adoption text)
Cummings et al., FSEC 1990: central Florida homes over 20 years old averaged about 17 ACH50, homes under 10 years about 8; return leaks about 10% of air handler flow
Green Building Advisor on Austin Energy audits (2009): 310 homes 10+ years old averaged 22% duct leakage
Texas A&M Energy Systems Lab 2002: typical DFW house of the 1990s modeled to Model Energy Code minimum with 10 SEER cooling
RhoeFlow plan v2, Era-based defaults for DFW table (claude/01-plan/research-and-plan.md); estimates to seed the questionnaire

ceiling_insulation_cavity_r.basis: Poor end: most 1980s Texas homes have R-19 attics and most 1990s homes R-30 (ResStock). Measure the depth in the attic and override.

wall_insulation_cavity_r.basis: R-11 batts in 2x4 walls, in about 90% of 1980s Texas homes (ResStock).

window_ufactor.basis: Double-pane clear glass in an aluminum frame, the most common window of the period in climate zone 3A (ResStock), at its code default U 0.80. Single-pane is next most common (U 1.20). Override from the label or spacer.

window_shgc.basis: Code default SHGC for double clear glass. Low-E glass is about 0.3 to 0.4.

air_leakage.basis: Estimate: Florida homes of this age measured about 8 (Cummings 1990); 1.15 to 1.5 times a post-2000 house (Chan 2013); ResStock median 10 to 15. A blower-door result replaces this.

duct_insulation_r.basis: R-4.2 flex in the attic (plan table; ResStock assumes R-4 before 2000). Read the jacket label.

duct_leakage_to_outside.basis: 15% of fan flow to outside (plan table), inside the 10% to 30% range ResStock assumes; low confidence. A duct-blaster result replaces this.
